subject: Capacity & SLO fit for Lighthouse Systems committed Dedicated tier
messages:
From: Emily Park <emily.park@lighthouse.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lighthouse.ai>, Gideon Clarke <gideon@lighthouse.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Jul 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity request — committed tier sizing and SLOs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week. Lighthouse is preparing the final commitment language (we're targeting the committed Dedicated tier) and procurement asked us to lock in an initial capacity plan so legal & finance can run numbers. High level profile below:

- Committed tokens/month: 3.5B tokens
- Peak concurrency: ~120 concurrent sessions during US business hours (13:00-17:00 UTC)
- Typical prompt+completion length: 2.5k tokens average (burst up to 8k in a small subset)
- Desired P95 generation latency <= 300ms for conversational flows
- Model: internal eval suggests LLM-v3-7B (we'll share model spec soon)

Can Redwood provide a short capacity/latency fit (tokens/sec numbers, suggested GPU slab counts for committed capacity + recommended burst pool) so we can include that in the SOW appendix? We also need a simple statement on headroom (how many spare GPUs / % buffer you recommend for safe SLAs).

If it's helpful, procurement is looping Gideon and they can share the draft SOW.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — can we get a slide or spreadsheet by EOD Friday?

Best,
Emily
Emily Park
Head of Integrations | Lighthouse Systems
[Attachment: draft_sow_lighthouse_v1.docx (docx, 45KB)]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@lighthouse.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 13 Jul 2028 09:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — committed tier sizing and SLOs

Emily — thanks, good to be moving fast. Looping Ben (capacity modeling) and Laura (SLO/pricing lead) — they'll run the numbers and produce a short workbook. A couple quick clarifying questions to tighten the model:

1) Can you share the traffic distribution by hour (UTC) for a typical weekday? Peak concurrency alone doesn't capture burstiness — are bursts uniform across sessions or dominated by a small % of users?
2) For the 8k bursts, are those sustained multi-turn sessions or one-off long completions?
3) Any hard constraint on cold-starts (e.g., need warm KV cache for near-zero added latency)?

Preliminary back-of-envelope: assuming LLM-v3-7B with optimized kernels, on an L40-type GPU we usually see ~750-900 tokens/sec single-stream for short context, and ~300-450 tokens/sec for longer contexts with KV pressure. For planning I recommend we model three execution profiles (short: 500 t/s, mid: 320 t/s, long: 180 t/s) and then size committed slabs conservatively on mid-profile with burst pool covering long-session peaks.

Ben/Laura — can you capture these profiles in the workbook and include a headroom column (recommended 20–35% buffer depending on burstiness)?

I can also provide a simple note for procurement that Dedicated commitments include a configurable burst pool and automatic overage billing rules.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Solutions 
Redwood Inference
Office: +1 (415) 555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@lighthouse.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marcus_lin@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 14 Jul 2028 11:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — committed tier sizing and SLOs

Emily / team — attached is a compact workbook with scenario modeling and a short slide (x-sheet + png): Lighthouse_compute_model_v2.xlsx and SLA-diff-chart.png. Summary below; see sheet 'RecommendedCommit' for the math.

Executive summary (recommended committed + burst architecture):
- Baseline assumptions: use mid-profile tokens/sec = 320 t/s (represents mixed 2.5k avg context with KV usage). Model-specific tuning can move this +/- 20%.
- Committed pool recommendation: 18 L40-equivalent GPUs (this produces ~5.76M tokens/sec aggregate at 320 t/s * 18 GPUs) which maps to ~3.1B tokens/month at our service factoring in avg token length and utilization assumptions.
- Burst pool: add a shared burst pool of 6 GPUs (on-demand) that can be used during peaks; automatic scaling with burst-rate caps to protect other tenants.
- Headroom: 25% headroom baked into committed sizing (in addition to burst pool). This matches a P95 latency target of 300ms under our simulated weekday peak (see sheet 'PeakSim').

Hardware-perf notes (approx):
- L40 (compute-optimized): 320 t/s at mixed 2.5k context (quantized execution still provides ~210 t/s)
- A100-80GB (older fleet): ~220 t/s at mixed workloads (higher variance on KV-heavy sessions)
- For the small subset of 8k sustained sessions, assume effective t/s ~110–130 (long-context slowdown). For that cohort we recommend routing to reserved warm instances to avoid P95 spikes.

Cost & contract implications:
- Committed 18 GPUs + 6 burst GPUs gives a predictable monthly RU (reserved units) price. I'll call out an overage rule we recommend: bursts beyond 6 GPUs billed at on-demand rate with a soft cap (we'll set an auto-fallback to smaller model variants if on-demand usage exceeds X hours).

Open questions / risks:
- If Lighthouse needs <10ms cold-start for every turn, committed warm-only routing will require sticky warm slots for a subset of sessions and increases committed GPU needs by ~12% (see sheet 'ColdStartImpact').
- Model variance: until we get LLM-v3-7B perf curves in our infra, +/-20% perf uncertainty exists; we recommend a 60-day review after go-live to reconcile actual tokens/sec and adjust slab counts.

Attachments: Lighthouse_compute_model_v2.xlsx (workbook with scenarios), SLA-diff-chart.png (visual p95 latency vs committed GPUs).

[Attachment: Lighthouse_compute_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 88KB)]
[Attachment: SLA-diff-chart.png (png, 180KB)]

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Capacity Planner | Redwood Inference

From: Emily Park <emily.park@lighthouse.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@lighthouse.ai>, Gideon Clarke <gideon@lighthouse.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jul 2028 08:55:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity request — committed tier sizing and SLOs

Thanks, Ben — this is exactly what procurement needed. A couple quick asks before we move to SOW: 

1) Can Redwood draft a one-page mutual action plan that includes the committed 18 GPUs + 6 burst pool, the 25% headroom note, and a 60-day reconciliation clause (we'll include a placeholder for the hourly overage cap)? That will slot into our SOW appendix.
2) Gideon — procurement: can you confirm whether Lighthouse wants the burst pool to be pre-authorized (automatic use up to 6 GPUs) or manually approved for each event? We want to align on billing behavior.
3) Jonas / Laura: please highlight the fallback policy (auto-model-fallback to a 3B variant if on-demand exceeds cap) in the mutual action plan language so legal can see operational controls.

If you can send the MAP + a short cost delta snapshot today we'll push the SOW through internal review and route DocuSign.

Thanks — looking forward to finalizing.

Emily
Emily Park
Head of Integrations | Lighthouse Systems
